Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios

# OC Manager

> OpenCode all-in-one workbench: making AI programming more elegant

**OC Manager** brings OpenCode's command-line operations into a handy desktop window: start services, manage sessions, browse projects, and edit configuration, all in one place. Supports OpenCode **v1 and v2**.

---

## What it can do

### One window, a clear workflow

- Left project tree, center conversation area, and right info panel: a three-column layout that is easy to follow
- Start services, switch sessions, and browse projects and files, all in the same window
- Multi-session tabs run in parallel on desktop. The top tab bar stays visible, each tab scrolls and renders independently, switching is smooth, and closing a tab releases its resources

### Clean conversations, key points stand out

- User and AI messages are laid out in separate columns
- Reasoning, tool calls, and file operations are collapsed by default; expand them when you want to see them
- Full Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting for code blocks
- Subtasks and to-do items are automatically extracted from sessions and presented in one place
- The command palette opens with the `/` key

### Files and Git, all in one place

- Lazy-loaded file tree; text, code, Markdown, HTML, images, and PDF can all be previewed
- Files can be edited, uploaded, and deleted
- Files can be opened in a separate window for focused browsing
- Changes are shown as side-by-side diffs, with the right side editable and savable
- The Git panel supports viewing changes, staging and committing, and pushing and pulling, and can connect through a proxy

### Configuration and skills, managed centrally

- **System Configuration** in the bottom-left corner manages interface appearance, network, web service, shortcuts, and about information
- Network and web service share the same dialog; it is read-only while the service is running and editable after it stops
- OMO model mapping is configured per agent or category
- Plans can be exported, imported, saved to the library, and applied in one step
- Provider model lists can be fetched with one click
- Project-level configuration: directly manage core settings, skills, commands, rules, and `AGENTS.md` under `.opencode/`
- Skill management: global aggregated scanning, conflict detection, one-click enable and disable, and symlink import

### Knowledge base, accumulated as assets

- Save ideas, operation steps, prompts, and project information as entries
- Organize entries with category trees and tags; Markdown editing with live preview
- Type `@` in a conversation to reference an entry, which is passed to the AI as independent context
- Entries can be converted into skills, commands, rules, or project guidelines with one click, with a preview and confirmation before anything is written

### Desktop details

- Stays in the system tray; click to toggle show and hide
- `Shift+X` brings up the main window at any time
- Launching a second time activates the existing window instead of starting another process
- Service status is pushed in real time via SSE; reconnects automatically after a disconnect and backfills missed messages; one click checks for new OpenCode versions
- Light and dark themes (one-click toggle in the mobile top bar), network proxy, and a visual directory picker

---

bluechonk/modelmux.body:
# modelmux

**One endpoint that takes over the quotas of multiple AI clients.** It consolidates channels such as AStudio, WorkBuddy, Qoder, Loomy, LobsterAI, Raccoon, TRAE, and CatPaw into **one OpenAI-compatible endpoint**, exposing the real models from each channel's catalog as `<channel>/<model>` pool IDs (the requester chooses the channel). It focuses on one thing: `npx modelmux` starts the gateway, and any OpenAI-compatible client pointed at it can use it. Login, multi-account pools, auto check-in, and quota refresh all run automatically inside the gateway.

## What it is

- **One gateway**: listens on `127.0.0.1:4412` and serves `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`, and `/health`.
- **Dynamic model pool**: externally, model IDs take the form `<cid>/<model>` (e.g. `loomy/kimi-k2.6`), and `/v1/models` aggregates the normalized results of every channel's `catalog` in real time. Clients select a channel explicitly with the channel prefix; same-named models in different channels are separate IDs.
- **Multi-channel routing**: each channel is a pool (model catalog + credentials + upstream protocol), registered under `packages/core/channels/`. The number of channels is determined by the **registry** (`mx model list` shows the full list), and the docs do not hard-code a number.
- **Channel chosen explicitly by the request prefix**: the `<cid>/` segment of the pool ID determines which channel is used, with at most one candidate. The ledger only serves as **health observation** and does not decide routing. Accounts whose quota is exhausted enter “cooldown” (restored automatically when it expires). Accounts with consecutive failures are circuit-broken and then automatically probed in half-open state, with exponential backoff on failures.
- **Fully automated operations**: signature-based login (QR code / device code / SMS, depending on the channel), **multi-account pools** (switch / remove / per-account quota), **auto check-in** (each channel's own daily reward), **quota refresh for all channels in parallel every 3 minutes**, and daily catalog refresh.
- **Zero third-party runtime dependencies**: implemented in TypeScript, with an empty `dependencies` in the shared layer. The web dashboard is hosted by `mx web`.

## Directory

```
packages/
├── cli/                      CLI entry point (bins modelmux / mx; registers all channels, then hands off to the shared CLI)
├── ui/                       Web admin dashboard (React 19 SPA, hosted by `mx web`)
└── core/                     Server-side runtime
    ├── gateway/              Shared layer (gateway / daemon / paths / channel registry)
    └── channels/<cid>/       One channel = one pool (model catalog + credentials +…

cttt-des/AI-BackpackBattles.body:
# Backpack Battles AI (背包乱斗 AI)

An external toolkit for the game Backpack Battles (背包乱斗): **battle log exporter** (read-only game memory → battle reports in the same format as the game), **battle simulator** (combat simulation based on reverse-engineered ground truth), and **external AI** (automated play). It does not modify any game files.

## ⚠️ Known Issues (Read Before Use)

The simulator does not yet fully match the game. The following **known issues** currently exist:

1. **Dragon Knight (黏黏龙骑士) cooldown fast-forward has positive-feedback amplification.**
   The mechanism itself has been reproduced 1:1 from the source code (each time an item on the board activates, DK's cooldown advances by 15%), and the linked loops for Twine (60% chain activation) and Chili (heat acceleration) have also been restored. However, the simulator's random number sequence differs from the game's, so small differences in the loop bonuses are amplified exponentially (measured: DK's attack interval decays to 0.02s, while the ground truth is stable at 0.35s+). Full convergence requires frame-by-frame alignment with the game's rng sequence.

2. **Some item effects still deviate.**
   The behavior of 518 items is executed via transpilation from unpacked source code, but the values, trigger timing, or condition checks of some individual items still differ from the game's actual behavior.

3. **Do not use simulator battle results as precise win-rate references for the game.** The automated acceptance probes (short, fixed-scenario test cases) cannot cover signal timing issues that appear in real battles. Several serious issues were found by comparing against recorded battle logs while all tools were passing.

If you find a problem, feel free to open an issue (attach the lineup JSON and seed so it can be reproduced exactly).

## Downloads (Releases)

Packaged standalone EXEs are published on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/cttt-des/AI-BackpackBattles/releases). No Python environment is required:

| Version | File | Description |
|------|------|------|
| **v0.4.0** | [`BackpackSimulator.exe`](https://github.com/cttt-des/AI-BackpackBattles/releases/download/v0.4.0/BackpackSimulator.exe) | Battle simulator (lineup battles / Monte Carlo win rates / item synergies / game-format battle reports) |

This repository uses the `Contents.hhp` project, the `Contents.hhc` table of contents, and the `Index.hhk` index in the root directory. Open the project in HTML Help Workshop and compile it. New pages and resources should be registered under `[FILES]`, and the table of contents and index updated accordingly. Generated CHM files are not under version control.

HTML/HTM files and these three project files are kept in GBK encoding. Body characters that GBK cannot represent are written as HTML numeric entities to avoid losing characters. Page declarations must match the actual encoding, and internal site links use relative paths. New pages should retain this page's errata entry. For related maintenance and check functions, see `scripts/feedback-entry.ps1`.

The entry point for the Spell Compendium (万法大全) is `2 万物万法万律/SpC万法大全/封面.htm`. Spell English names can be searched from the CHM index. Online details require an internet connection.

## CHM "Preface" Section

This document is a set of D&D 3rd edition expansion rules (3R, and 3e material to be gradually added) translated by players themselves. The copyright of the Chinese translations belongs to their respective translators. This document merely organizes the translated materials and, as far as possible, ensures consistent layout and naming to facilitate study and reference.

You will find in this book a large amount of publication material from other **world-setting resources**, **licensed third parties**, and so on. Its sole purpose is to help experienced players reduce the time and effort spent searching for resources in specific campaigns. We do not recommend opening all resources included in this book to your group without first skimming and understanding them, nor do we recommend that any player use the compendium's inclusion as grounds to urge your DM to open up too many resources.

In addition, please consider whether certain resources are highly tied to your campaign's background story. This may involve whether these resources should narratively appear in your campaign, whether they should be used by your players or monsters, and whether partial rewriting is needed to meet your story's needs. The compendium only includes existing translations. You may well need to consult the original text to confirm whether there are mistranslations, omissions, or misreadings. The compendium's production team is working to correct such errors, but human resources are limited, so when you encounter questions you are unsure of, please try to verify them yourself.

All translated articles included in the expansion compendium are provided solely as Chinese reference when comparing against the original rulebooks. Do not use them for printing or commercial purposes. For purchasing the original books, please refer to relevant online bookstores. If any article infringes your copyright, please notify us and we will remove it as soon as possible. …

emef2247/x68k_vgm2mml.description: Conversion from VGM to MDX MML
emef2247/x68k_vgm2mml.body:
# x68k_vgm2mml

This tool extracts performance information such as notes, note lengths, volume, and timbres from register operations recorded in VGM, and generates structured MML for X68000 (for MDX) and PCM IR.
Requires Python 3.10 or later.

## Usage

### Generate MML and PCM IR by specifying a VGM file

```bash
# Generate MML only
python vgm2mml.py INPUT.vgm --outdir OUTDIR
```

If you want to automatically perform everything from MML generation through MDX generation, use `scripts/export_mdx.py` (described below).

### Batch convert a directory containing VGM files to MML, PCM IR, and MDX/PDX

Specify the directory containing the VGM files to convert them in batch.

```bash
# Automatically converts not only to MML but also through to MDX/PDX.
python scripts/export_mdx.py INDIR --outdir OUTDIR --force
```

By default, the VGM's whole-song loop is not used, and an MDX that ends after one pass is generated (to help large songs fit within the limits). To render the VGM's whole-song loop as a second pass with saved state:

```bash
python scripts/export_mdx.py INDIR --outdir OUTDIR --force --vgm-song-loop
```

Generating MDX requires an MDX compiler such as MXC or mmlx. PDX generation uses soundlog.

For setting up these environments, see [Environment setup](https://github.com/emef2247/x68k_vgm2mml/blob/HEAD/docs/mdx_compiler_setup.ja.md).

To automatically install these external tools, use [scripts/setup_tools.sh](https://github.com/emef2247/x68k_vgm2mml/blob/HEAD/scripts/setup_tools.sh).

### Main options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--outdir OUTDIR` | Output directory for conversion results |
| `--force` | Skips and continues past unsupported performance elements or over-capacity PCM within the allowed range, with diagnostics |
| `--vgm-song-loop` | Renders the VGM's whole-song loop as a second pass with saved state (default is an MDX that ends after one pass) |
| `--no-song-loop` |…

# marble XNU —— iOS 16 kernel running on Redmi Note 12 Turbo

> **Must-read for audio/SMMU takeover:** [`docs/smmu-dead-ends.md`](https://github.com/jebbranch/ios-port-marble/blob/HEAD/docs/smmu-dead-ends.md) ——
> SMMU approaches already proven wrong, the correct register map, and the discipline of "stop using DATA_BUFFER as a probe".
>
> **Must-read for GPU takeover:** [`docs/gpu-probe.md`](https://github.com/jebbranch/ios-port-marble/blob/HEAD/docs/gpu-probe.md) (all on-device readings for v1–v30 and vendor kprobe traces), [`docs/gpu-gpt-question.md`](https://github.com/jebbranch/ios-port-marble/blob/HEAD/docs/gpu-gpt-question.md) (external Q&A draft), [`docs/gpu-feasibility.md`](https://github.com/jebbranch/ios-port-marble/blob/HEAD/docs/gpu-feasibility.md) (feasibility inventory).
> Device-specific handover and failure lists are maintained locally only and are not included in this repository.

Port Apple's open-source **XNU 8796.141.3** (the iOS 16 contemporary kernel) to **Redmi Note 12 Turbo (marble / SM7475 / Snapdragon 7+ Gen 2)**.
The boot method is **shim + `fastboot boot`, pure RAM execution**: no flashing `boot`, no writing to `userdata`, no modifying GPT. When the test ends, the kernel resets itself and the phone returns to TWRP/Android.

> Research project, for learning and experimentation only. Apple firmware/userland images are not distributed; do not treat this as a daily-use phone system.

## Current status

| Subsystem | Status |
|---|---|
| XNU early boot (16K pages / GICv3 / vtimer / framebuffer) | ✅ |
| UFS read/write, HFS+ root (tail of userdata) | ✅ |
| Touch / buttons / RTC | ✅ (touch has known limitations) |
| USB (enumeration / partial transfers) | 🟡 |

LightTickets is a self-hosted issue/ticket platform for Minecraft server management. It supports web-based management and connects with Paper/Folia and Velocity plugins for interaction.

- Issue management: Create issues from templates, and set tags, assignees, visibility, and other parameters

```text
LightTickets/
    ├─ backend/            # Backend service
    ├─ frontend/           # Web frontend
    ├─ plugin/             # Minecraft plugin integration
    ├─ docs/               # Some temporary documentation constraints, not official reference

    └─ docker-compose.yml  # Example docker compose file

- Node.js 24 and npm
- Java 21 or above (Minecraft plugin)

Install all dependencies:

```bash
npm install
npm install --prefix backend
npm install --prefix frontend

Start the service:

```bash
npm run dev
```

After startup, visit `http://localhost:23310`. Initialization is required on first run.

The backend API listens on `http://localhost:23320` by default.

Start only the frontend or backend:

```bash
npm run dev:server   # backend only
npm run dev:web      # frontend only
```

# dotfiles

> The dotfiles for fuckin' awesome development environment

## Supported environments

- macOS 26 or later (Apple Silicon only)

## Installation

First, open **System Settings > General > Software Update** and update macOS to the latest version.
On a new Mac or a Mac that was just reinstalled, the update catalog may be outdated, so you may not be able to update directly to the latest version.
In that case, use [the full installer](https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201475), or install the intermediate versions it offers, in order.

```sh
bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p-chan/dotfiles/main/scripts/install.sh)"
```

By default, the repository is cloned to `~/src/github.com/p-chan/dotfiles`.
When using a different location (CI, a temporary macOS environment, an existing checkout, etc.), specify `DOTFILES_DIR`.

```sh
DOTFILES_DIR="$PWD" bash scripts/install.sh
```

`install.sh` records this location as the `dotfiles.root` setting for mise in `home/.config/mise/conf.d/dotfiles-root.toml` (machine-specific and not tracked by Git).
As a result, you can run `mise bootstrap` afterward without setting any environment variables.
To change the checkout location later, move the directory, then re-run `install.sh` with the new path specified in `DOTFILES_DIR`.

## Herdr Claude integration

`mise bootstrap` installs the Herdr integration for Claude Code.
Herdr requires absolute paths in hooks, so the Git index keeps them in a portable `$HOME` form, and they are restored to local paths in the working tree.
The generated hooks remain local.

road-kid/dsh-qoder-plugin.body:
# dsh-qoder-plugin

[English](https://github.com/road-kid/dsh-qoder-plugin/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | **Simplified Chinese**

Connect models from your **Qoder subscription** to [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). Paste a personal access token (PAT) and you can select Qoder's models directly in DSH. No browser login flow is needed, and DSH's own conversation loop, compression, and permissions are unchanged.

The China edition (qoder.com.cn) and the international edition (qoder.com) are two separate entries, each with its own credentials, model catalog, and quota. They are never mixed. If you only use one edition, the other does not appear at all.

## What it does

- **Paste and go**: On the settings card, paste a PAT and click "Save". The plugin first validates the token against the matching region and saves it only if it passes. The model then appears in DSH's model picker, with no restart needed. You can later "Replace PAT" or "Clear PAT" at any time. A new token overwrites the old one only after it passes validation, so a mistyped paste will not lose a working credential.
- **Independent dual regions**: `qoder` (China edition) and `qoder-global` (international edition) each have their own credentials and model catalog. A token generated on qoder.com is invalid for the China region, and vice versa. The two never cross over.
- **Model toggles**: Lists all models for the edition line by line in Qoder's official order (not reordered). Each row shows its reasoning tier and the official default tier. Turning a model off hides it from DSH's model picker immediately.
- **Per-model context window selection**: Each model has its own bold solid slider, with the window tick marks that model declares shown below it. Dragging only changes a draft. On release, the slider snaps to the nearest available tier. Changes are committed when you click "Save" together with your other settings.
- **Three-level model catalog fallback**: The plugin fetches the list live first. When offline or after a restart, it falls back to the last saved catalog. If neither works, it uses a built-in list. The card states where the current list came from and can be refreshed manually in place.
- **Quota readout in the input box**: When the current session uses a Qoder model, `Qoder · remaining quota` appears in the input toolbar. Clicking it opens an anchored panel showing the plan, remaining / total, progress, and expiry time at a glance. When you switch to another model, the readout steps aside automatically.
- **Daily check-in**: You can claim 100 Credits per day. The claim window is **10:00 → next day 10:00 (UTC+8)**, not the calendar day. If you claim at 23:00, it still reads "checked in today" after midnight. The account card shows check-in status and remaining credits directly, with one-click claiming. You can also enable auto check-in in settings (off by default) and set a unified check-in time.
- **Multiple accounts**: You can save multiple PATs for the same edition and switch between them at any time. Each account's remaining credits and status appear directly in the list. Auto-switching, on by default, moves to the next available account in saved order when one account cannot be reached. All of these options are under "Settings / Advanced Settings". The defaults work without adjustment. …

# Songloft Player (Lynx)

The Lynx client for Songloft Player, completely rewritten from the Flutter version as ReactLynx + TypeScript. Supports Android / iOS / HarmonyOS / Web.

To learn about the underlying technology: [Lynx official website](https://lynxjs.org/) · [ReactLynx official documentation](https://lynxjs.org/react/).

"Settings → Playback settings → Keep screen on on lyrics page" is off by default and is saved only on this device. When enabled, the screen stays on while lyrics are visible (in wide-screen mode, lyrics are shown side by side). It remains effective while playback is paused. Returning to the cover, leaving the player, or switching to the background restores automatic screen-off. Android/iOS/HarmonyOS require a native installation package that includes the new screen-on interface; older shells degrade safely. On Web, it depends on browser Screen Wake Lock support and permissions; a denied request does not affect playback.

## Current status

The project is currently positioned as a **preview release**. Core playback, library/playlists, lyrics, plugins, themes, multi-server support, and admin settings are already implemented. The About page now separately provides client update checks and server update checks: dev only checks dev, and the stable release only checks the latest stable release. Native bundle updaters for all three platforms are integrated into the source. Android has completed local interface download/cancel/cold-start verification; compilation and device acceptance on iOS/HarmonyOS remain open. Signing keys for official updates are not yet configured. Old shells or incompatible updates offer an installation package entry for this channel. See [client update protocol](https://github.com/songloft-org/songloft-player-lynx/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/client-updates.md) for details. The native desktop client and the Bundle local backend are not in scope for this round.

The native device cache already has an identity/audio-track variant index, whole-playlist and multi-select batch tasks, and local management/offline playback entry points. Expired logins retain local-only access, and explicit logout hides the old identity. See [device cache](https://github.com/songloft-org/songloft-player-lynx/blob/HEAD/docs/reference/device-cache.md) for details. Android has actual file/interface verification; compilation and device acceptance on iOS/HarmonyOS remain open.

Web now provides playlist JSON import/export, supporting file selection, authentication refresh, download, and cancellation. When browser click permission expires, a main-thread control is provided. Chrome standalone/embedded at the root path has been tested; Firefox/Safari are pending verification. wycto/dsh-dock.body:
# dsh-dock · Feature Dock

**DeepSeek Harness feature dock plugin**: register and toggle all small features uniformly from one management panel.

Small features such as model balance, usage records, model settings, and the image understanding proxy are all gathered into one 'Feature Dock'.
Each feature is an independent module with a registry, a toggle, and error isolation. New features are added as new modules, and existing features are unaffected.

---

## Feature Overview

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| **Usage Records** | Records all LLM API calls: second-level time filtering, token and cost statistics (**configurable unit prices per model, persistently saved and billed by the user-entered prices**, supports multi-segment time-of-use prices and weekend/holiday off-peak prices, built-in peak/valley pricing plus automatic sync of official price lists as a fallback), grouped summaries, detail search, and CSV export |
| **Model Settings** | Edit the model catalog of each provider: input types (text/image with annotations) and thinking intensity levels. Image capability can be declared manually by you. After adding a new provider, the page automatically rereads the catalog on entry, and writes back to the official configuration with hot reload |
| **Model Providers** | Manage custom model providers themselves: add, edit, delete (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Messages, etc.), store API keys in the local credential store, and fetch the upstream `{baseURL}/models` list. Layout matches the official model management page. **Independent feature that can be disabled separately**. When disabled, the config write and outbound fetch routes are also turned off |
| **Model Balance** | Shows the account balance of all model providers (auto-refreshes every 5 minutes). Built-in 'DeepSeek Account' official-site balance uses the host login session, with top-ups and gifts shown separately. This is not an API key balance endpoint |
| **Task Animations** | 19 task-running animations (including Stellar Expedition, Nebula Tide, Warp Channel, Quantum Radar, Constellation Network, Deep Sea Pulse, Neural Circuit, etc.). Speed is linked to task activity, and all settings are persisted |
| **Task Notifications** | Notifications for task completed / error / needs confirmation / needs answer / stuck. The settings page supports a 'server-side config / local config' master switch and an event × channel checkbox matrix. In-page cards have a master switch, independent toggles for completed/error/needs confirmation/stuck, and three card detail levels: concise/moderate/detailed. Stuck cards state the main/sub task, stall duration, and last action, and auto-dismiss on recovery. A main task waiting on a sub task is not falsely reported. **Stopping in place to wait for a human (waiting for approval or for an answer) is never counted as stuck**. Waiting for an answer shows a separate 'Task needs your answer' card. Includes 6 notification sounds, browser system notifications, and voice announcements (**two layers: server master switch plus local switch**. The server controls the whole instance, the local switch is stored in the current browser, and announcements play only when both are on. Completed/stopped/needs authorization/needs answer/stuck × concise/moderate/detailed × optional voice). DingTalk/Feishu group bot push (sent directly by the host, works even when the browser is closed, message detail adjustable). Independent of animations, each can be started or stopped separately |
| **Run Status** | Overview of task running status: phase / elapsed time / turn / step / tool / … of in-progress tasks |

yoqu/gonggong-space.description: Self-hosted group chat for AI coding agents: @ a Bot and Claude Code / Codex works on a teammate's machine, preview results right in the chat. @ a Bot in the group, and Claude Code / Codex on a teammate's machine gets to work.
yoqu/gonggong-space.body:
[English](https://github.com/yoqu/gonggong-space/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | Simplified Chinese Help manual: [Chinese](https://yoqu.github.io/gonggong-space/) · [English](https://yoqu.github.io/gonggong-space/en/) Demo environment: [http://gg.uyoqu.com](http://gg.uyoqu.com/) (default environment; register an account to try it directly, no self-hosting needed) 共工空间 is a self-hosted AI collaboration platform for small teams. Each member connects their own machine, and Claude Code / Codex on that machine becomes a **Bot** that anyone in the group can @. People and Bots discuss, assign tasks, and hand off work in the same group. The process, changes, and results are visible to everyone. ## Video introduction ## Why we built it - **Context scattered across individual terminals**: You had Claude change an interface, but a teammate's Codex doesn't know about it. In the group, even messages that don't @ a Bot are passed to it as context, so everyone shares the same background. - **Machines sitting idle**: Your work machine has the repository, dependencies, and a logged-in Agent, but teammates can't use them. Once bound, group members can @ your Bot directly and work on your machine. - **Results are invisible**: The Agent says "it's already running," but the service only listens on `localhost` on its own machine. 共工空间 tunnels it to the browser so the whole group can open it and look. ## Highlights | | | | --- | --- | | 💬 **Group chat as command center**
@ someone to start work; follow-up messages can interrupt and add to the task; `/stop` halts at any time. A Bot can hand its task off to another Bot in the group. | 🖥️ **Runs on your own machine**
The daemon only connects outward, so home NAT and corporate firewalls aren't a concern. Model calls are sent directly from the member's machine and don't go through the server. | | 🌐 **One-click result preview**
Web pages, API services, static reports, desktop app windows, and WeChat Mini Program simulators can all be opened and operated directly in the group, and time-limited public links can be generated. | 🔍 **Transparent process, auditable changes**
Thinking, tool calls, and command output stream back in real time. Diffs, Git status, and file trees are easy to check, and each turn's token usage and context occupancy are clear at a glance. | | 🛡️ **Permissions and approvals**
Three tiers: read-only / workspace write / full access. Only the Bot's owner can approve out-of-scope actions. When a Bot is unsure, it asks the group a multiple-choice question. | 🇨🇳 **Works out of the box in China**
Defaults to the npmmirror registry. The daemon can install Node, Claude Code, and Codex in one click. Built-in presets for mainstream model vendors mean you only enter a Key after choosing a vendor, and CC Switch configurations can be imported. | ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR… ```

znq19/KiraAI_video_comprehension_plugin.description: Let your Bot watch videos too. QQ, Bilibili, and local videos can be sent to the matching model for analysis, either in native multimodal mode or frame-extraction mode, for detailed understanding. Includes Bilibili video download.
znq19/KiraAI_video_comprehension_plugin.body:
# Video Comprehension Plugin

KiraAI video comprehension plugin: automatically detects QQ video messages, compresses them, extracts frames at three levels, and analyzes them as a collage; **speech transcription** (Bilibili official subtitles take priority, and it can be skipped when the model has built-in audio and video understanding); supports Bilibili link download, sending, search, AI summary, and **html5 direct-link passthrough**; 4 independently configured model groups (native video / frame extraction / built-in audio and video understanding); supports local videos and time-range analysis.

## Core Capabilities

1. **Automatic video message detection**: recursively scans the message chain (**including quotes `Reply.chain` and merged forwards `Forward.chains`, with multi-level nesting supported**) → `raw_message` → **proactively calls `get_msg` by message ID**, as a three-level fallback
2. **Automatic caching of received videos**: downloads a video locally as soon as it is detected, and tells the bot the path in the next conversation turn (`auto_cache_video`, enabled by default; the caching scope is controlled by `cache_scope`, which defaults to caching only videos that were @-mentioned, quoted, or wake-triggered)
3. **Speech transcription**: converts the audio in a video into **timestamped text** and passes it to the model along with the video (both `native` and `frames` modes include it); **Bilibili official subtitles take priority**; can be skipped with one setting when the model has built-in audio and video understanding (`native_audio`)
4. **Compression pipeline**: ffmpeg scaling plus CRF compression, keeping the duration unchanged
5. **Three-level frame extraction**: scene-change frames → I-frames → uniform fill frames, maximizing information density
6. **Collage and timestamp annotation**: each frame is labeled `MM:SS.mmm [I/P] #N`, and multiple frames are composed into a collage arranged in chronological order
7. **Multi-model routing**: 4 independent configuration groups, with `frames` and `native` **strictly isolated** (the frames group never receives video_url); selected automatically by priority and duration; `native` (sends the video) or `frames` (sends the collage). **Can be specified by name**: "Analyze with Agnes using frame extraction" → the bot passes `model="Agnes"`
8. **Session management**: first-turn analysis plus follow-up questions (`session_id`); a new video automatically switches sessions; **model stickiness** (follow-ups default to the model group used for the first analysis)
9. **Time-range analysis**: the bot can specify that only seconds N~M be examined, with multiple segments in one request supported (up to 5 segments, each ≤300 seconds)
10. **Bilibili capabilities**: automatic link download and sending (0 tokens), search, AI summary preferred, download by quality, html5 direct-link passthrough; **video sending is open to all adapters that declare `video` support, including QQ / QQ Official / Telegram / Discord / WeChat / WebChat (plain-text adapters such as Bilibili dynamic posts clearly indicate that they do not support it)**
